gloss: start of autumn; first day of autumn

definitions.gloss: start of autumn; first day of autumn
definitions.explanation: one of the 24 solar terms ({二十四節気|にじゅうしせっき}) in the traditional East Asian calendar, marking the beginning of autumn, usually falling around August 7-8

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}の{立秋|りっしゅう}は{八月|はちがつ}{七日|なのか}だ。
examples.english: This year's start of autumn is August 7th.

examples.japanese: {立秋|りっしゅう}を{過|す}ぎても、まだ{暑|あつ}い{日|ひ}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: Even after the start of autumn, hot days continue.

examples.japanese: {立秋|りっしゅう}を{過|す}ぎると{暑中見舞|しょちゅうみま}いではなく{残暑見舞|ざんしょみま}いになるので、{時期|じき}に{気|き}をつけよう。
examples.english: After the start of autumn, summer greetings change from 'mid-summer greetings' to 'lingering heat greetings,' so pay attention to the timing.

notes:
One of the {二十四節気|にじゅうしせっき} (24 solar terms) used in the traditional calendar. Despite the name, {立秋|りっしゅう} falls in early August when temperatures are still at their peak in Japan, so it marks the calendrical rather than the meteorological start of autumn.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {立秋|りっしゅう}を{迎|むか}える: to reach the start of autumn
- {立秋|りっしゅう}を{過|す}ぎる: to pass the start of autumn
- {立秋|りっしゅう}の{候|こう}: seasonal greeting phrase used around this time

CULTURAL NOTE:
{立秋|りっしゅう} has practical significance for seasonal greetings. Before {立秋|りっしゅう}, summer greeting cards are called {暑中見舞|しょちゅうみま}い. After {立秋|りっしゅう}, they must be called {残暑見舞|ざんしょみま}い instead. Sending the wrong type is considered a social faux pas.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {立春|りっしゅん}: start of spring (around February 4)
- {立夏|りっか}: start of summer (around May 6)
- {立冬|りっとう}: start of winter (around November 7)
